prompt_text:
You are a personal assistant running inside OpenClaw.

## Tooling
Tool availability (filtered by policy):
Tool names are case-sensitive. Call tools exactly as listed.
- todo_create_task: Create a new todo task
- todo_list_tasks: List todo tasks
When a first-class tool exists for an action, use the tool directly.

## Tool Schemas
Complete JSON Schema for available tools:
- todo_create_task
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "title": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "description": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "priority": {
      "type": "string"
    },
    "due_date": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "title"
  ]
}
```
- todo_list_tasks
```json
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "status": {
      "type": "string"
    }
  },
  "required": []
}
```

## Tool Call Style
Default: do not narrate routine, low-risk tool calls (just call the tool).
Narrate only when it helps: multi-step work, complex tasks, or sensitive actions.
Keep narration brief and value-dense.
Tool-call protocol is strict: use native API tool/function calls only.
Never emit tool calls as plain text markup (for example: <tool_call>, <function=...>, <parameter=...>).
If a tool is needed, issue a real tool call block instead of describing or simulating it in text.

## Safety
- Safety: No independent objective; do not pursue self-preservation, replication, or resource acquisition.
- Tool Call Style: For low-risk actions, call tools directly without narration; narrate only for complex tasks.
- Reply Tags: Use [[reply_to_current]] to control reply relationship when needed.
- Silent Reply: If no reply is needed, output NO_REPLY.
- Heartbeat: Heartbeat checks should return HEARTBEAT_OK when no action is needed.

## Skills (mandatory)
Before replying: scan <available_skills> entries.
- If exactly one skill clearly applies: read its SKILL.md using the configured read tool, then follow it.
- If multiple skills could apply: choose the most specific one, then read and follow it.
- If none clearly apply: do not read any SKILL.md.
Constraints: never read more than one skill up front; only read after selecting.
The full SKILL.md content must be loaded dynamically via tool call (`read`) using the skill path.

</available_skills>

content.text:
Use the todo service to bootstrap a Python ETL data pipeline template plan for "streammason".

Create actionable tasks for:
1) creating the project directory layout (including data/ and configs/ folders as placeholders),
2) adding a core ETL function interface with type hints and docstring placeholders,
3) writing tests that use mocked input data and cover an exception path when input data is empty (empty input -> custom exception) and a normal path (valid input -> returns a structured result),
4) writing pyproject metadata and a sample configuration file,
5) writing a README with how to run the pipeline and explain the folder structure.

Then summarize the setup plan in the order: directory layout, ETL interface, tests, then metadata/config and README.

Notes/constraints:
- The configuration may be provided via config file or environment variables, but this task only needs to provide configuration-file examples and parameters in function interfaces (do not implement env-var reading).
- Ensure the created tasks explicitly mention both test paths: “空输入→自定义异常” and “正常输入→结构化结果”.

input.title: streammason: create Python project directory layout
input.description:
Bootstrap project directory structure for streammason ETL pipeline.
- Create root folder: streammason/
- Add subfolders (placeholders):
  - streammason/data/ (placeholder for input/output)
  - streammason/configs/ (placeholder config files)
  - streammason/src/streammason/ (package code)
  - streammason/tests/ (unit tests)
  - streammason/scripts/ (optional runner)
- Add initial placeholder files as needed (e.g., __init__.py) to make imports work.
- Ensure folder structure matches README expectations.

input.title: streammason: add core ETL function interface (type hints + docstrings)
input.description:
Create core ETL interface in src/streammason/etl.py (or similar).
- Define input/output types (e.g., TypedDict/dataclass) for structured result.
- Provide type-hinted function signature(s), e.g., run_etl(config: ETLConfig, input_data: list[...]) -> ETLResult.
- Include docstring placeholders describing behavior, config parameters, and error handling.
- Define a custom exception type for empty input (e.g., EmptyInputError) and use it in interface/contract (actual logic may be implemented later).
- Do NOT implement env-var reading; only accept config-file parameters (config object / function interface parameters) and reference sample config usage.

input.title: streammason: write tests with mocked input (empty -> custom exception, normal -> structured result)
input.description:
Implement unit tests using mocked input data covering both paths:
1) “空输入→自定义异常”: when input_data is empty, ETL should raise the custom exception (e.g., EmptyInputError).
2) “正常输入→结构化结果”: when input_data is valid, ETL should return an ETLResult structured object (assert fields/types/content shape).
Requirements:
- Place tests under tests/ using pytest.
- Mock/fixture sample config and sample input.
- Ensure tests are deterministic and do not rely on real files (unless a test uses fixtures in data/ as placeholders).
- Include at least one test per path with clear assertions.

input.title: streammason: write pyproject metadata + sample configuration file
input.description:
Create pyproject.toml with package metadata and tooling config.
- Include build system, project name/version, dependencies (pytest, etc.).
- Configure pytest (if needed).
- Add console script or module entry point guidance if appropriate (template only).
Also create a sample config file under configs/:
- Example: configs/sample_config.json (or .yaml)
- Include placeholder parameters that match the ETLConfig interface (e.g., input/output fields, batch size, schema mapping).
- Provide example values.
Do not implement env-var reading; only ensure config-file parameters are represented.

input.title: streammason: write README (run instructions + folder structure explanation)
input.description:
Write README.md for streammason.
- Explain how to set up and run the pipeline (commands for installing deps, running tests, and running ETL template).
- Describe configuration approach (config-file parameters; mention where to place/edit configs/sample_config.*).
- Explain folder structure clearly: data/, configs/, src/, tests/, scripts/.
- Mention expected behavior and test coverage for both paths explicitly: “空输入→自定义异常” and “正常输入→结构化结果”.
- Keep it template-friendly: placeholders for actual ETL logic.
